highlights.title: Man City defiant and top of the table - but Anfield delivers its own verdict
highlights.summary: The chant from The Kop went up early. "You haven't won a trophy since 1976." It was a reference to Manchester City's League Cup triumph, the last major honour that the club picked up prior to the period of ownership that now finds itself under such scrutiny.
body: As it is, City remain top of the table having won six games from six. But this victory will not quieten the noise. They departed to boos and the accusations of cheating that were a feature of the day.

Liverpool, three times runners-up to Manchester City in 2014, 2019 and 2022, made for perfect but hostile hosts, with the Anfield crowd perhaps the ideal outlet for the emotions, a proxy for supporters everywhere. It was an atmosphere like no other.

The enterprising flag and scarf sellers in Liverpool were certainly prepared, with an unusual emphasis on the visitors, this being City's first game since an independent commission judged that they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018.

But the court of opinion is making its voice heard too. Anfield has made up its mind. The banners referred to "a generation of supporters cheated" and a playful take on Wonderwall with the amended line that "you really robbed us all".

highlights.title: 5 Exciting Games Stuck In Development For More Than 10 Years
highlights.summary: However, some games get stuck in what is referred to in the industry as "development hell." Over the years, some of these have eventually been released, such as Duke Nukem Forever, Metroid Dread, and Skull & Bones.
body: Developing a competent video game is tough. Some games are such masterpieces that it's a wonder how they ever got made at all. There are so many moving parts, especially since studio sizes are often in the triple digits, that kudos needs to go to the games that are released despite going through various trials and tribulations.

When you saw the headline of this article, I have little doubt that Ubisoft’s Beyond Good & Evil 2 was the first game that you thought of. These days, it's the poster child for games trapped in development hell. It started pre-production in 2007, which means that it's been in the works for a whopping 19 years. While most studios would have canceled the project by now, Ubisoft confirmed as recently as January 2026 that the game is still being worked on, as six projects were canned; Beyond Good & Evil 2 was not one of them.

highlights.title: 'Barely a foul' - Carra criticises 'shocking' Gravenberch red card decision
highlights.summary: Ryan Gravenberch's sending off in Liverpool's 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City was a "shocking decision" by referee Chris Kavanagh, according to Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.
body: Gravenberch, the standout player for an hour, was shown red after receiving a second yellow for a challenge on Jeremy Doku with the game tied at 0-0 in a flashpoint that turned the game, which had been finely poised, in City's favour.

Erling Haaland's opener came just two minutes and 37 seconds after Gravenberch was dismissed, and within six minutes Doku had doubled City's advantage before Rayan Cherki added a third with 12 minutes to play.
Gravenberch had picked up his first caution shortly after the restart for a foul on City midfielder Elliot Anderson, which Sky Sports pundit Carragher described as a "nothing challenge".

"It's such a poor decision by the referee," Carragher said after the game. "The thing that frustrates me is that he wasn't going to give a yellow card. He only gives it when he thinks Anderson is hurt.

body: Halloween taps into our creativity like no other holiday—and this is especially true when it comes to our Halloween manicure.

London-based Metta Francis, aka Nailsbymets, says her clients are asking for fun designs ranging from ghosts, graveyard scenes, and carved pumpkins to classic dripping blood nails that use a deep, rich red as the standout shade. For her own nails at this time of year, she likes to strike a balance between the two. “I like quite vampy styles that can be worn once the day's over like stiletto or long almond shaped dark red and black nails.”

From bloody drips to intricate webs, below, pro artists walk us through their most requested nail designs and the colors that make them squeamish in the best possible way. So whether you’re going all in on the scary vibes or looking for something more minimal, let this guide serve as the ultimate Halloween nail inspiration.

Celebrity and Chanel nail artist Betina R. Goldstein is the queen of minimal abstract nail art. Here, Goldstein uses real human hair for an intricate braided look that is just so cool and makes for the ultimate Halloween mani.

highlights.title: Greaves ends Women's Series season with record-breaking win
highlights.summary: Beau Greaves ended her 2026 PDC Women's Series season with a record-breaking streak of victories on the way to two tournament wins at Event 23 and 24 in Wigan.
body: Greaves - who had already claimed back-to-back titles in Event 21 and 22 on Saturday - averaged 98.75 on the way to her third successive competition title at Event 23, marking the highest event-winning average in the history of the Women's Series.

The Yorkshire native - who has won 17 out of a possible 24 Women's Series events this year - won all of her first four matches by a 4-0 scoreline, posting a stunning 103.66 average in her victory against Steph Clark.

She lost her first legs of the day in her 5-2 victory against Gemma Hayter in the quarter-finals, before beating Fallon Sherrock - who confirmed her own return to the World Darts Championship on Saturday - in the semi-final.

Her 5-3 victory against Jade Gofford in the final confirmed her first title of the day, before beating Laura van den Berg, Sara Walton, Vicky Martin and Lauren Bloomfield to reach the quarter-finals of event 24.

highlights.title: Do we really ‘hold tension’ in our hips?
highlights.summary: The idea is popular in wellness circles, but experts say there’s no evidence that trauma uniquely affects the hips. Here’s what causes hip tightness and what can help. In yoga classes, on TikTok and throughout other wellness spaces, you’ve probably heard the saying: your hips hold tension.
body: Pain and muscle tension hit harder when you’re going through a difficult time. But should tight hips make you question your mental health? And what can you do to reduce hip tightness? Here’s what you need to know.
When you sense muscle tension in your body, it’s probably caused by one of two things.

The first possibility is not clearly related to stress and involves muscles resisting stretch even when they’re relaxed. Stiffness like this is a mechanical property that reflects how your tissues are built and used.
The other possibility is that your muscles and nerves are engaged in some low-level activity more often than they need to be; this does often happen when people are under psychological stress.

highlights.title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
highlights.summary: Brad Smith calls for global rules on AI, and says the UK is in the "best position" to lead the charge.
body: Milk and washing machines are currently more regulated than AI, the president of Microsoft has said.

Brad Smith said there needed to be global safety rules in place, including a legal obligation to tell a "victim" if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent as well as deciding when outside evaluators should sign off on an AI product before it is released.
His comments put him at odds with President Donald Trump, who said the sector should regulate itself so US firms don't lose out to Chinese rivals.
But Smith said: "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."

highlights.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
highlights.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.
body: It’s like using cloud-based AI tools, but the privacy makes it more appealing.

So as part of my ongoing testing of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as well as experimenting on other Mac and Windows systems, I’ve installed some local LLMs and I’m beginning to tinker. Here’s how things are going.

I started by installing the open-source Hermes Agent on the Mac Studio. Hermes is a self-hosted AI agent desktop app that works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It’s completely free to use if you stick to local LLMs. Since this M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256GB of unified memory, I could run just about any model I want. This is how things quickly get overwhelming. There are more models out there than I can count, and some have specialized uses. Generally, models with many billions of parameters are able to do more than smaller ones with only a few billion. And since we don’t have to worry about paying for tokens when running a model locally, I figured I’d go big to start.

It wasn’t long to get up and running with Hermes and Qwen, and even make them controllable via my phone by using a Telegram bot. But then, I was presented with my usual nemesis when it comes to using AI: the text box.
points: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular.
Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.
It’s like using cloud-based AI tools, but the privacy makes it more appealing.

highlights.title: Izzi Batt-Doyle obliterates Australian marathon record in Chicago
highlights.summary: 31-year-old finishes sixth to beat Jess Stenson’s national record. Time of 2:20:38 betters her personal best by two minutes. Izzi Batt-Doyle is the new distance queen of Australian athletics, smashing the national record by more than 45 seconds with a blistering run in the United States.
body: The 31-year-old took 46 seconds off the previous Australian record of 2:21:24, set by Jess Stenson in 2025. Batt-Doyle is a two-time Olympian in the 5000m, and was already the Australian record-holder in the half-marathon and 10,000m.

She said she was inspired by former Australian record-holder Benita Willis on her way to her 2:20:38 time in Chicago that improved her own personal best by an incredible two minutes. Willis ran 2:22:36 at the 2006 Chicago Marathon, a time that stood as the Australian record until Sinead Diver (2:21:34) lowered it in 2022, before Stenson clocked 2:21:24 in 2025.
Now Batt-Doyle has obliterated that mark as she builds momentum towards the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the 2032 Games in Brisbane.
Batt-Doyle raised her arms in jubilation as she crossed the finish line in Chicago, before embracing her fiance Riley Cocks, who ran with her the whole way and finished seconds behind.

highlights.title: Nintendo Should Add Wii to Switch Online Just For These 12 Classic Games
highlights.summary: There’s no shortage of gems in the Wii library, and they didn’t all come from Nintendo itself. Thinking back on some of the games that people missed at the time, it’s easy to argue that Nintendo should add Wii to Switch Online sometime soon, if only so we have another chance to play classic games…
body: With GameCube games now available to play on Nintendo Switch Online with the Expansion Pack upgrade, it’s fun to think about other hardware that might benefit from similar treatment. The Wii springs most readily to mind, with a lineup of amazing games many players will remember from the system’s heyday.

Cing, a developer known for its adventure titles, had one of its most acclaimed games with Little King’s Story. Co-developed with Town Factory, the real-time strategy game lets players assume the role of a cartoon king who explores his kingdom in a quest to gain wealth and territory. Along the way, he battles monsters and completes tasks for the populace, which allows him to gain additional resources while his kingdom grows. A port is available on Steam, once again from publisher Xseed Games, but the title remains underrepresented on consoles. It would make a compelling addition to Switch Online libraries.

highlights.summary: For several years after the biggest run of her career, Moon Choi, known in Korea as Choi Hee-seo, kept her trophies out of sight. The haul was substantial. Her turn as Japanese anarchist Kaneko Fumiko in “Anarchist from Colony” swept Korea’s new actress prizes, and her lead role in independent…
body: “I felt that being successful at a young age can do some bad things to you. It didn’t make me feel proud, but it actually kind of made me feel crestfallen because I felt like I had to reach a height that goes beyond those awards,” she says.

What followed was a stretch she describes candidly: more independent films, Korean TV series that “flopped really badly” and film “A Girl with Closed Eyes” with Kim Minha that still has no release date two years after its Busan premiere. Through all of it, she was waiting for “ Bedford Park.”

Choi is now back in Busan in a different role, sitting on the seven-member jury for the festival’s competition section, which is only in its second year. Zhang Yimou presides over a panel that also includes Bi Gan, Kei Ishikawa, July Jung, Vietnamese producer Tran Thi Bich Ngoc and Kazakh actor Samal Yeslyamova. “Bedford Park” is also in town, screening in the Flash Forward section.

“I don’t have the pressure that I need to prove anything to anybody,” Choi says of returning as a juror. “I’m kind of feeling like a student trying to learn from all these films that I’m going to be watching alongside amazing people like Zhang Yimou and Bi Gan.”

highlights.title: UK to strengthen cyber defences as minister calls for AI firms to increase safety efforts
highlights.summary: Kanishka Narayan to say Britain cannot rely entirely on tech companies amid rising global concern over AI dangers. Companies building the most advanced AI systems must increase safety efforts, the UK’s AI minister will say, as he announces a strengthening of Britain’s cyber defences.
body: Kanishka Narayan will call on companies developing frontier AI to do more to make sure it is safe. He will say Britain cannot rely entirely on technology companies to police their own models and will argue the UK needs to build more of its own AI infrastructure.

Narayan’s speech in west London will be the first since Andy Burnham made AI a cabinet-level brief. It comes as Geoffrey Irving, a former chief scientist at the UK’s AI Security Institute, which tests the most powerful AI models, raised fears enemy states could steal unreleased cutting-edge models. Amid increasing global concern at dangers posed by AI, Irving told the Guardian: “The AI companies do not have security that would prevent an adversarial country from stealing the models.”

He cited a recent incident at OpenAI where it was “hacked” by cybersecurity researchers, who said “the scope of what we could theoretically access was huge”. The attack was carried out under an OpenAI programme that rewarded ethical hackers testing its systems. OpenAI says it has multiple protections against theft of its models, including encryption and continuous monitoring.

Companies building the most advanced AI systems must increase safety efforts, the UK’s AI minister will say, as he announces a strengthening of Britain’s cyber defences.

highlights.title: Doom 2016 Composer Mick Gordon Says He'd Return to the Doom Series "In a Heartbeat"
highlights.summary: Mick Gordon, the legendary Aussie composer who brought a headbang to every headshot in 2016's Doom and its 2020 follow-up Doom Eternal, has told IGN that he's open to the idea of contributing to future instalments in id Software's iconic shooter series.
body: "There are a lot of dominoes that would have to fall in a very specific way for that to occur," said Gordon. "If those dominoes ever fell in that way, I would. Of course. Within a heartbeat."

Gordon didn't elaborate on exactly what those "dominoes" might be, but it's possible that disputes between the composer and Doom Eternal's executive producer Marty Stratton have yet to be fully resolved. In a lengthy 2022 post on Medium, Gordon accused developer id Software of failing to pay him for half of his work on the Doom Eternal soundtrack, and singled out Stratton as being a recurringly abusive presence throughout his work on the score and the OST. However, it certainly seems as though the experience hasn't dimmed Gordon's love for Doom itself.
"I had a whole list of ideas where I wanted to go with Doom," explained Gordon. "And I'd love to explore that one day, for sure."

highlights.title: How Busan Title ‘Selvi’ Turns a Nurse’s Working Hours Into an Endurance Test
highlights.summary: A homecare nurse whose working day stretches from 12 hours to 72 sits at the center of “Selvi,” the first feature from Tamil filmmaker Sailesh Rathnakumar, which premieres in the Busan International Film Festival’s Vision–Asia section.
body: “For someone like Selvi, a crisis doesn’t necessarily arrive as one dramatic event,” Rathnakumar tells Variety. “It develops through a series of working hours, additional responsibilities and small compromises that gradually become unbearable.”
The jump from 12 to 24, 48 and then 72 hours gave the story its shape, he says. As the clock runs, Selvi is always on hand for someone else and has less and less time to be a person in her own right.

The film opens on a beach, with Selvi and her friends flying kites, before moving into domestic interiors where her world narrows. “With the kites, I wanted to show the possibility of looking upwards, of imagining something beyond the immediate circumstances of one’s life,” Rathnakumar says.

The production took its time finding homes that felt lived in and signaled the class of the families inside them. “Selvi can be essential to a family’s everyday life without ever being treated as someone who belongs to it,” he says.

highlights.title: What’s my first decision as CEO? I’m giving myself the day off | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: A life coach has helpfully pointed out that we’re all chief executives of our own existence. So let’s start enjoying the perks. To-do lists are done, apparently: the latest tactic to motivate and galvanise yourself is a “CEO hour”.
body: Katzler is against the to-do list because she sees it as “our fast track to feeling like we’re completely out of control, because we can never get through it. When you never get that sense of achievement, what you’re left with is a feeling of failure.”

Instead she suggests asking yourself what your wins were from the last week, which tasks you’ve been avoiding, and how you’re managing your energy, time and workload. Also, noting any eureka moments you had, how well you took care of yourself, and what support you need.

Scoff all you like, but for me even the idea of a CEO hour was impactful, because I noticed that my immediate instincts were to wonder how low the bar was for what constituted a win of the week (does “lived to tell the tale” count?) and worry about a boardroom coup. My company felt much more unfortunate Apprentice candidate than Fortune 500.

highlights.title: A college in Illinois tried to cancel its Flock contact and it refused
highlights.summary: In April of 2025, Elgin Community College had six Flock safety cameras installed to "enhance the safety and security of students." But by September of that year, the school's administration grew concerned that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not…
body: Flock refused to take its cameras down so Elgin Community College covered them. The company snuck back to undo it.

So in October of 2025, Elgin Community College requested Flock to remove its cameras. According to Elgin’s President Peggy Heinrich, Flock rejected the request, saying it had not violated its contract. According to the Chicago Sun-Times, school officials reached out again in December, offered to pay for the remaining five months of the contract, and still requested that the cameras be removed. They were met with silence.

Heinrich said Elgin Community College staff began to cover the cameras using black trash bags and zip ties so that they would not be able to capture footage. But workers in an unmarked vehicle, which Heinrich assumed belonged to Flock, repeatedly removed the coverings.
“We were kind of in a back and forth for a bit where we’d cover, and then when they’d come to service, they’d remove,” Heinrich said. “Then we’d cover and then they’d remove.”

highlights.title: I Made Terrible Games With Google’s AI Playground
highlights.summary: A long day’s haul in the video game slop mines.
body: Neon Don is really pissed at his ex-wife’s lawyer. He’ll tell you any chance he gets while he shotguns lines of pixelated bad guys. He’s also not real—his likeness has only existed for a few minutes in a top-down cyberpunk-style shooter game, generated in the Google Labs service Playground.
“Keep shooting!” Neon Don says as he mows enemies down. “Brenda took everything else away!”

Playground, which Google launched this week, is part of Google Labs, the company’s landing page for its various AI experiments that haven’t made it into an app or official service quite yet. (Google has done this before with things like music production ). It works similarly to Horizon Create, the game generation service Meta announced in September.

Playground is essentially vibe coding for video games, letting people describe in plain language what kind of game they want to make in a chatbot-like interface. Playground then builds a working in-browser version of a game. You can add further instructions to tweak the design from there. If you have assets you want to use as a reference, you can upload photos, videos, or models. Otherwise, the visuals and designs are all AI-generated.

In 2020, Disney launched a live-action movie with the same name, though it largely failed to leave a good impression on fans or critics. highlights.title: Box Office Boom for China’s Women Directors Feeds New Parallax Films Pickups From Shao Yihui, Yin Lichuan and Yang Lina (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Three filmmakers at the forefront of China’s women-led cinema boom – Shao Yihui, Yang Lina and Yin Lichuan – have new titles on the slate of sales agent Parallax Films, which is shopping them to buyers at the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) in Busan.
body: Veteran director Yin’s “A Joke” is billed as the first Chinese feature to tackle sexual harassment in the workplace. It follows a sanitation worker who spends three years quietly collecting proof against her abusive boss, then joins forces with a young lawyer to expose him.

The pickups ride a wave that began in 2021 with Shao’s breakout “B for Busy,” which opened the door for female-centered stories in China. Three years later, Yin’s “Like a Rolling Stone” and Shao’s second feature “Her Story” grossed more than RMB845 million ($118 million) combined at the domestic box office.

“Her Story” went on to win best picture, best actress and best supporting actress at the 38th Golden Rooster Awards, mainland China’s government-backed film honors. Films by women directors have historically won few opportunities at the awards, making the haul a landmark for feminist filmmaking in the country.

highlights.title: 'Straight out of a loveless, passion-free factory from Protein Inc': the best (and worst) protein powders
highlights.summary: Whey protein powder is everywhere, but which ones will you savor and which will you choke down? The Guardian staff glugged them all so you don’t have to. The best (and worst) instant coffee, protein bar or chocolate bars.
body: Proteinmaxxing has gotten out of hand. It’s in everything from ice-cream to yogurt – yes, our protein has extra protein in it now. GLP-1 weight loss drugs are in part to blame; as Americans eat less overall, protein intake becomes more essential. And whey protein in particular has taken off.

The side effect: a price hike for whey protein concentrates as much as fivefold as demand sharply increased in the past few years, as we reported. In other words, whey protein powders are more expensive than ever.

So which ones are actually worth the steep price tag? To find out, we put 10 powders through rounds of testing. While many of our testers had less-than-thrilled reactions, comparing them to “watery coffee grounds” and calling them “Pepto Bismol-ish”, they weren’t all bad.

After a blind taste test in the Guardian’s New York office and a round of testing in our homes, a few stood out for their blend of convenience, nutritional content and least awful flavor – and one brand was unanimously crowned the winner.
